classes.class: A guard's path scope is narrower than the concept it protects, so research or the order path drifts under a green guard

Cheapest single detector for this class: fail when a '# allow-silent:' marker appears in a file the guard cannot scan - a suppression for a guard that cannot fire is proof of the mismatch, and it surfaced 55 today.

classes.class: An alert is emitted but never reaches outcomes.jsonl, so it pages nobody
classes.structural_fix: A CI check that every _send-style alert module also writes outcomes.jsonl. This is the THIRD instance: CLAUDE.md already documents the identical delivery defect twice (ib_stop_over_cover, bybit_over_cover), which is exactly why those two appear in the ERROR feed and the exit-eval breach does not.

classes.class: An armed gate's soak cannot settle the decision the arming exists to inform

hypothesis_tested.hypothesis: The defects that keep recurring are caused by guards that do not work - i.e. the CI guard suite produces greens that are not evidence, and tightening the guards is therefore the highest-leverage fix.
hypothesis_tested.evidence: main is GREEN across all 92 run_guards entries when run ungated (PASS 90 - FAIL 2 - SKIP 0, both failures environmental: lint-imports absent, and pr-landing's documented pre-declaration state). 54 of 79 guard scripts carry a failure-path self-test and ALL 54 were EXECUTED this pass and exited 0; bucket (b) - 'mentions a self-test but only exercises the happy path' - is EMPTY by measurement, not by assumption. Two named defect classes were verified genuinely SWEPT with working positive controls: order_packages.id declarers 0 over 90 files (control: 42 files DO match the probe), and the one-sided-coverage class 1 surviving occurrence of 5, that one being the documented-legitimate carve-out. So the guards are real and largely proven. The defects instead cluster at SEAMS and in UNARMED RUNTIME INSTRUMENTS: the two committed invariant suites both pass planted-control self-tests and neither has a scheduled caller. REFUTING this hypothesis is the most useful output of the pass, because it redirects effort away from adding CI guards - which is what the repo has been doing - and toward arming instruments that already exist. A SECOND hypothesis was also tested: CLAUDE.md's assertion that 'every recorded repeated-mistake class has an executable prevention' - it is SUPPORTED, 5 of 5 classes name a prevention and all 7 named script paths exist AND are referenced in run_guards.py - and it is VACUOUS, because the load-bearing word is 'recorded': 85 backlog rows self-declare a recurrence and ZERO cite a ledger class.
